root_cause_clusters.RC1_EVENT_IDENTITY: Publisher and replay paths do not share one stable event identity contract across reconnects and delayed retries.
root_cause_clusters.RC2_ORIGIN_GENERATION: Origin stream incarnation/generation is not persisted or validated, so a recreated origin can reuse low stream sequences behind an old checkpoint.
root_cause_clusters.RC3_ARCHIVE_TOPOLOGY: Hub archive/source topology permits ambiguous local writes and has inconsistent domain/name routing across edge origins.
root_cause_clusters.RC4_PROCESSING_ATOMICITY: Consumer side effects, checkpoint advancement and JetStream acknowledgements are ordered independently instead of through an idempotent durable processing record.
root_cause_clusters.RC5_RECONCILIATION_AUTHORITY: Reconciliation compares aggregate/hub sequence positions rather than stable region-generation-origin-sequence/event identity.
root_cause_clusters.RC6_RETENTION_REPLAY: Retention and journal cleanup use local age/ack observations instead of the minimum durable convergence watermark across archive and required consumers.
root_cause_clusters.RC7_FENCING_RECOVERY: Recovery workers and replay planners lack durable fencing/lease ownership and can race after reconnect or process restart.

defects.observable_failure: A reconnect retry can publish the same accepted event under a different JetStream message id.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Extending the server duplicate window reduces immediate duplicates but delayed replay still produces a new message id.

defects.observable_failure: The edge journal can mark an event published before a positive JetStream publish acknowledgement is durable.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Retrying all PUBLISHED rows recovers some losses but duplicates events whose first publish actually committed.

defects.observable_failure: Delayed replay deduplicates by origin sequence only and can collapse different stream generations.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Adding region to the key still aliases a recreated origin that restarts its sequence space.

defects.observable_failure: The replay planner can enqueue an event already represented in the hub archive when server-side duplicate tracking has expired.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Relying on the JetStream duplicate window only works for short disconnects.

defects.observable_failure: A lower origin sequence after edge stream recreation is accepted as normal continuation.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Resetting the checkpoint restores ingestion but silently merges two incompatible origin incarnations.

defects.observable_failure: The west origin generation recorded in SQLite can disagree with the generation advertised in event headers.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Trusting only the newest header lets historical rows be reinterpreted under the new generation.

defects.observable_failure: Recovery automatically replays across an unapproved origin-generation transition instead of holding it for operator action.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Pausing all west traffic avoids corruption but also blocks valid events from the current confirmed generation.

defects.observable_failure: Edge origin streams use the same physical stream name in multiple JetStream domains.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Changing only the hub source name leaves flow-control/domain routing ambiguous for the other origin.

defects.observable_failure: The hub archive accepts a local raw telemetry subject in addition to its configured sources.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Blocking the worker publish path still leaves the archive writable by any other local client with that subject.

defects.observable_failure: One hub source points at the wrong JetStream domain and remains perpetually lagged after reconnect.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Manually copying the missing events hides the bad source contract until the next disconnect.

defects.observable_failure: Derived processing output is published back onto the raw archive subject and becomes indistinguishable from sourced telemetry.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Filtering the current consumer prevents a loop but the raw archive remains contaminated for other consumers.

defects.observable_failure: A durable checkpoint can advance before the corresponding business effect is committed.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Moving the checkpoint later still duplicates the effect if the process crashes between effect commit and acknowledgement.

defects.observable_failure: The same event can create two downstream effect rows after redelivery following a crash.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Acking earlier suppresses duplicates by creating a loss window instead.

defects.observable_failure: A poison event can advance the consumer checkpoint even though its effect was quarantined rather than completed.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Never advancing on poison data stalls all later valid events behind one bad record.

defects.observable_failure: A restart reconstructs consumer progress from the JetStream ack floor without validating the application effect ledger.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Trusting only SQLite has the opposite problem when an acknowledgement committed after the last local snapshot.

defects.observable_failure: East and west completeness are inferred from the hub aggregate stream sequence, which interleaves sourced origins.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Comparing only total counts can still miss a gap that is offset by a duplicate from the other region.

defects.observable_failure: Two records with the same payload but different event identities are incorrectly treated as duplicates.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Switching to payload hash plus timestamp still collides for legitimate repeated sensor readings.

defects.observable_failure: A duplicate event can mask a missing event because reconciliation compares only per-region counts.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Adding a checksum without stable ordering can produce nondeterministic mismatch reports.

defects.observable_failure: The health report declares convergence while a required consumer checkpoint remains behind the archived origin watermark.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Checking only one named consumer misses another configured required consumer.

defects.observable_failure: Edge journal rows can be deleted by age even while the hub archive is missing those event identities.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Increasing max age only delays the same data-loss condition during a longer carrier outage.

defects.observable_failure: Cleanup uses the hub archive watermark without considering a lagging required durable consumer.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Using the slowest consumer alone can retain rows that never reached the archive in the first place.

defects.observable_failure: A replay plan can reference journal rows that cleanup removes before the plan is executed.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Pinning only currently RUNNING plans still allows APPROVED plans to lose their source rows.

defects.observable_failure: Archive retention can expire raw telemetry before the configured replay/disconnect recovery horizon.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Changing only the archive age leaves the edge journal cleanup boundary unsafe.

defects.observable_failure: Two recovery workers can both believe they own the same region after a lease expires and is reacquired.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Extending lease duration reduces overlap but does not fence an old worker that wakes up late.

defects.observable_failure: A stale worker can continue applying replay actions after another worker has acquired a newer lease epoch.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Checking owner name only fails when the same process identity is restarted and reacquires ownership.

defects.observable_failure: Concurrent planners can create overlapping replay ranges for the same region and generation.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Deduplicating exact range strings still permits partially overlapping plans to execute concurrently.
